title: Randy's Smothered Pork Chops
imageAlt: Smothered pork chop with mushroom gravy, rice, and vegetables
summary: Bone-in chops with mushrooms, onions, and gravy. Next time: one-hour bake, creamier gravy, and mashed potatoes.
ingredients: 4 bone-in center loin pork chops, about 1 inch thick
1 large yellow onion, sliced into ¼-inch half-moons
½ cup whole milk or half-and-half
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Season the pork chops with salt and pepper.
Brown the chops in a skillet with a little butter or oil for 2–3 minutes per side. They do not need to cook through.
Remove the chops. Cook the onions for 2–3 minutes, then add the mushrooms and cook another 4–5 minutes.
Stir in the cream of mushroom soup, onion soup mix, beef broth, milk, and Worcestershire sauce. Scrape up the browned bits from the skillet.
Place the chops in a baking dish, pour the gravy over them, and cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 1 hour. Check for tenderness and doneness; add only 5–10 minutes if truly needed.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve over mashed potatoes with plenty of gravy.

journal.general: The first attempt baked for 1 hour 15 minutes and was slightly dry and tough near the bone; the outer meat was perfect. Keep the generous mushrooms and onions. There was plenty of gravy.

title: Mississippi Pot Roast
imageAlt: Mississippi pot roast served over mashed potatoes with pepperoncinis
summary: Rich, tangy chuck roast served over creamy mashed potatoes with plenty of pepperoncinis.
steps: If time allows, remove the roast from the refrigerator 20–30 minutes before cooking.
Pat the roast dry with paper towels and season lightly with black pepper. Do not add extra salt because the seasoning mixes are already salty.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the roast for 2–3 minutes per side, including the edges, until deeply browned. Do not cook it through.
Place the browned roast in the slow cooker.
Sprinkle the ranch seasoning and au jus gravy mix evenly over the roast.
Place the stick of butter on top.
Add the whole pepperoncinis around the roast and pour in the pepperoncini juice.
Cover and cook on LOW until a fork slides in easily and twists the meat apart. Begin checking around 6 hours, but cook longer as needed.
If the roast is still firm late in the cook, switch to HIGH and check again after 45–60 minutes.
Shred or pull apart the tender meat and stir it into the cooking juices.
Serve over mashed potatoes with extra cooking juices and sliced pepperoncinis.

journal.general: ★★★★★ Randy Favorite. The first test used a 2.47 lb chuck roast. Cook to tenderness rather than strictly by the clock: if a fork can lift the roast without pulling it apart, it needs more time. The center became tender before the thicker outer portions, so continue cooking until all sections pull apart easily. The flavor was spot on. Next time use more pepperoncinis, add sliced pepperoncinis to each serving, and save every drop of the cooking juices for gravy and reheating leftover mashed potatoes. Served with mashed potatoes boiled exactly 18 minutes and finished with a hand mixer.

cookLog.author: Randy
cookLog.note: Flavor was outstanding. The center became tender first, while the thicker outer portions needed more time. Use more pepperoncinis next time and add sliced pepperoncinis when serving.

title: Randy's Simple Mashed Potatoes
summary: Simple, creamy mashed potatoes with butter, warm milk, and sour cream.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon salt for the cooking water, plus more to taste
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into roughly 2-inch chunks.
Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water, and add about 1 tablespoon salt.
Bring to a boil and cook for 18–20 minutes, until a fork slides into the potatoes easily.
Drain well. Return the potatoes to the hot pot over low heat for about 1 minute to dry them slightly.
Add the butter, warm milk, and sour cream.
Mash until smooth, then season with salt and black pepper.
Stop mashing as soon as they are smooth so they do not become gluey.

journal.general: Made to serve under Mississippi Pot Roast or smothered pork chops. Excellent fresh and reheats well with a splash of milk. Even better with leftover pot roast juices or homemade gravy.

cookLog.author: Randy
cookLog.note:
Boiled exactly 18 minutes.
Butter first.
Warm milk.
Hand mixer.
Excellent.

title: Breakfast Sliders
summary: Hawaiian rolls layered with scrambled eggs, ham, white cheddar, bacon, and spinach, then baked until golden.
ingredients: 12 dinner rolls or Hawaiian sweet rolls
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Slice the rolls in half horizontally, keeping the tops and bottoms together as two slabs.
Place the bottom slab in a 9 x 13-inch baking dish.
Spread the scrambled eggs evenly over the rolls, then layer on the ham, white cheddar, bacon, and spinach.
Place the top slab of rolls over the filling.
Brush the tops with melted butter and sprinkle with black pepper.
Bake for about 20 minutes, until the tops are golden and the cheese is melted.
Cut into 12 individual sliders and serve warm.

journal.general: La Jefa requested these again, so they are automatically a favorite. Adapted from Tasty's Breakfast Sliders recipe. Take our own photo next time and record any changes Randy and Lisa prefer.

title: Randy's Camp Breakfast Tacos
summary: Built at home, finished over the campfire. Crispy tortilla, bacon, eggs, cheese, and plenty of picante.
steps: Cook the bacon until crisp. Drain and chop into bite-sized pieces.
Scramble the eggs in butter until just barely set. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Allow the bacon and eggs to cool for about 10 minutes.
Divide the eggs, bacon, and cheese evenly among the tortillas.
Roll each burrito tightly, folding the ends in as you roll.
Wrap each burrito individually in heavy-duty aluminum foil and refrigerate overnight.
At camp, place the foil-wrapped tacos over medium-low grill heat or indirect campfire coals.
Turn every 3–4 minutes for 12–15 minutes until heated through.
Open carefully and add plenty of picante sauce before eating.

journal.general: Designed for camping. Assemble everything at home so breakfast at camp is almost effortless. Let the eggs cool slightly before rolling so the tortillas stay firm. Heavy-duty foil works best. Picante sauce isn't optional—it gets added after opening the foil at camp.
